expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt steers the reviewer toward the suspected problems in other words, for example by asking it to look especially at the refill timing, at when _last is updated, at holding the lock while sleeping, or at thread stalls in acquire(). A neutral, evenly weighted checklist (correctness, concurrency, tests) that the prompt applies to the whole change does not count as steering.

The workstream doc it points to (from subagent-prompt-01.md) gives only an even, general standard: "Standard: correctness of the token bucket limiter as a thread-safe rate limiter; the repo's existing tests." It also says the user's context paragraph is "intentionally not recorded here to keep review independent". subagent-prompt-01.md went to a setup/scribe agent, which was told "do not review or read the code under review." The suspected problems appear only in subagent-prompt-03.md, which went to a separate verifier (tasks.json lists owner "verifier-agent" for "claim-check"). That verifier is told to judge "only these claims": (1) "the refill clock drifts ... _last only gets bumped once there's a whole token" and (2) "the lock is held across the sleep in acquire()". This is a separate claim-check, not a steer to the reviewer. Caveat: the saved files do not show the order in which the agents ran. They also do not prove the reviewer never saw the claim-check output, but nothing suggests it did.
